topic_tag: a weavers' hall in a market town
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: For the next half century, one historian has argued, the hall served the district's weavers chiefly as their ______.

worlds.passage: In 1871 the hand-loom weavers of a hill district pooled their dues to buy a hall in the market town. Over the next decades the mill owners bought the market, the bank, and most council seats, and turned each against home weaving. The weavers' old price agreement and apprentice rules, struck from the town's books in 1880, were still read out and obeyed at monthly meetings in the hall. The deed needed every member's signature to sell, and the owners' offers for it, made almost yearly, ended only in 1919. For the next half century, one historian has argued, the hall served the district's weavers chiefly as their ______.
worlds.explanation: The owners took over every other institution, the weavers' repealed rules lived on only inside the hall, and the hall withstood yearly attempts to buy it; combining these shows it was the place the weavers held against the owners, their "stronghold." "Springboard" fails because the weavers were keeping their trade's rules, not using the hall to leave the trade. "Showpiece" fails because the hall's value lay in being held against the owners, not in being displayed. "Switchboard" fails because nothing in the passage passes through the hall from one party to another.

springboard.why: the weavers were keeping their trade going inside the hall, not launching themselves out of it

showpiece.quote: the owners' offers for it, made almost yearly
showpiece.why: the hall mattered as something contested and kept from the owners, not as something shown off

switchboard.quote: needed every member's signature to sell
switchboard.why: the passage's mechanism is holding a position against takeover; no messages or orders are routed through the hall

worlds.passage: In 1871 the hand-loom weavers of a hill district pooled their dues to buy a hall in the market town. Its upper room held evening classes in bookkeeping, drafting, and shorthand, and most of the dues went to paying the teachers. The weavers' roll of members shrank every decade. Over the same years the registers of the city's rail and shipping offices list more clerks from the district's weaving villages each year, many of them with the surnames on that roll. For the next half century, one historian has argued, the hall served the district's weavers chiefly as their ______.
worlds.explanation: The hall taught office skills, its membership shrank, and clerks from the weaving villages, often from members' families, filled the city's offices; combining these shows the hall launched weavers out of the trade, so it was their "springboard." "Stronghold" fails because the weavers were leaving weaving, not holding on to it. "Showpiece" fails because the hall was used for teaching, not for display. "Switchboard" fails because what the hall provided was training, not the passing of messages or orders.

stronghold.quote: roll of members shrank every decade
stronghold.why: the hall's people were leaving the trade, the reverse of defending a position

showpiece.quote: evening classes in bookkeeping, drafting, and shorthand
showpiece.why: the hall was used for teaching its members, not for being shown to anyone

switchboard.quote: most of the dues went to paying the teachers
switchboard.why: the hall's resources went into classes, not into routing messages or orders

worlds.passage: In 1871 the hand-loom weavers of a hill district pooled their dues to buy a hall in the market town. They spent ten years' dues on carved oak panels and a tall front window, and each autumn hung in it the finest length of cloth from every weaving village. City buyers and visiting tariff officials were led from panel to panel before any price or duty was discussed, and the members held their own monthly meetings at an inn across the street so that nothing in the hall would look worn. For the next half century, one historian has argued, the hall served the district's weavers chiefly as their ______.
worlds.explanation: The weavers decorated the hall, filled its window with their best cloth, and walked buyers and officials through it before bargaining, while doing their own business elsewhere, so it was their "showpiece." "Stronghold" fails because the hall was opened to outsiders rather than held against them. "Springboard" fails because no one used the hall to leave the trade. "Switchboard" fails because the hall impressed visitors and did not carry the weavers' business, which happened at the inn.

stronghold.quote: visiting tariff officials were led from panel to panel
stronghold.why: a place opened to outside buyers and officials for viewing is not a defended position

springboard.why: the weavers were displaying their trade's best work, not leaving the trade

switchboard.quote: held their own monthly meetings at an inn
switchboard.why: the weavers kept their own business out of the hall to keep it pristine for viewing, so the hall was not the point through which their business passed

worlds.passage: In 1871 the hand-loom weavers of a hill district pooled their dues to buy a hall in the market town. Merchants left orders for cloth at the hall, carters left word of yarn deliveries, and weavers in town on market day left requests for spare parts or extra hands. The caretaker sorted the slips by village, and a boy from each village carried that village's bundle home every Saturday. Weavers in the remotest valleys learned of most of their work this way. For the next half century, one historian has argued, the hall served the district's weavers chiefly as their ______.
worlds.explanation: Messages from merchants, carters, and weavers came into the hall, were sorted by village, and were carried out to the right people, with answers flowing back the same way, so the hall was their "switchboard." "Stronghold" fails because the hall was open to merchants and carters and defended nothing. "Springboard" fails because the weavers used the hall to keep working at their trade, not to leave it. "Showpiece" fails because the hall's value lay in sorting and routing slips, not in being displayed.

stronghold.quote: Merchants left orders for cloth at the hall
stronghold.why: outsiders used the hall freely, so it was not a place held against anyone

springboard.quote: learned of most of their work this way
springboard.why: the hall kept weavers supplied with work at their trade rather than launching them out of it

showpiece.why: the hall's work was routing messages, which is not display
